audit_scope.description: Prague BLAKE2F precompile execution, EIP-7685 execution layer to consensus layer request framework, EIP-7872 local builder blob limit configuration, and EIP-2 Homestead fork signature validation and difficulty adjustment

in_scope: BLAKE2F precompile (0x09) input validation and execution
EL request generation and requests_hash commitment (EIP-7685)
Local builder blob limit configuration and block construction (EIP-7872)
Contract creation gas semantics (53,000 initial gas)
Request validation and processing from EL (EIP-7685)

misclassified_entities.reason: This represents a smart contract already executing within the EVM that calls the BLAKE2F precompile. It is not an external entity; it is internal code running inside the EL execution environment. The true external entity is the transaction submitter that initiated the execution.

This represents a local configuration file on the node operator's machine. It is not an external entity crossing a trust boundary in the protocol sense; it is a local trusted input under the operator's control.
Fork protocol parameters are hardcoded constants defined by the protocol specification. They are not external entities; they are intrinsic to the system and do not cross a trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC / P2P Mempool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions arrive from unauthenticated external sources. For EIP-2: signature s-values must be validated (s <= secp256k1n/2). For EIP-7685: transactions may trigger request generation via system contracts. For BLAKE2F: transactions may invoke the precompile with arbitrary input data. All transaction content is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Physical Network Environment
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network conditions are fully outside system control and can be adversarial. An attacker could degrade bandwidth to cause block propagation failures. EIP-7872 mitigates this for local builders by allowing blob limit configuration, but the network environment itself remains untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitters via P2P Mempool
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p blob transaction gossip (EIP-4844 type-3 transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob transactions arrive from unauthenticated P2P peers. The blob data and transaction parameters are untrusted. Builders must select blobs within their bandwidth budget to ensure successful propagation. Blob gas pricing and inclusion priority are subject to manipulation.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction signatures must have s-values <= secp256k1n/2 (EIP-2 Homestead rule). High s-values must be rejected to prevent transaction malleability. Note: the ecrecover precompile (0x01) intentionally still accepts high s-values for legacy compatibility.

BLAKE2F input must be exactly 213 bytes. The final flag byte must be 0 or 1. Gas cost is rounds * GAS_BLAKE2_PER_ROUND and must be checked before execution. The rounds parameter is attacker-controlled and determines computational cost; gas metering must accurately reflect this.

Request generation occurs during transaction execution via system contracts. The requests_hash in the block header must be computed as SHA256 of sorted, filtered, individually-hashed requests. EL must correctly accumulate all requests and the commitment must be verifiable by the CL.

Network bandwidth constraints may prevent timely block propagation if too many blobs are included. Builders must configure blob limits appropriate to their bandwidth capacity. A minimum floor of 1 blob must be enforced to prevent zero-blob configurations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Mempool blob transaction selection for block building
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blob transactions in the mempool are untrusted. Builders must validate blob transaction format and select blobs within the effective limit (min of protocol max and user-configured max). Blob data availability must be ensured before block propagation.
